summary: Spec fidelity: the scenario atip.claim14.15 still says each stated 1.4 size is the 0.36.0 measure and 'a live answer is not larger than it and lies within a tenth of it, the patterns of 0.37 being shorter' (.canon/specs/kind=feature/area=atip/claim14.feature:167), but 79815f634 changed its bound test (changelog_problems, atip_claim14.rs) to accept a live answer a tenth either way, because 0.38 made 'schema finding close' larger (live 3,965 against the stated 3,739: +6.0%; finding list 1,225 against 1,201). The sentence was not reworded, so scenario-diff.md does not list it and the independent review of atip.claim14.15 stays current on a Then step the test no longer pins ('not larger'), and no flow of the finding-closer brief authorises the change. Reword atip.claim14.15 to the tenth-either-way rule (and name 0.38) so a reviewer reads it again, or keep the old bound by recording the sizes again. The documented 0.36 claim itself holds: finding close 3,965 < 16,212 and finding list 1,225 < 3,998 of 0.35, sum with the tree 29,882 < 38,421, and the finding list sum is still larger (27,142 against 26,207) with its sharing-rule reason. Blast radius: the tolerance is anchored to the 0.36.0 numbers, so finding close has 4% (about 150 bytes) of headroom left; the next option or help text added to it fails the test again.
